data.body: A subagent sharing its parent's MCP connection passes as_agent; the server's called_from is the PARENT's harness worktree, so claim adopted it (adopt_existing) and bound the subagent's item to the parent's tree and branch; the next subagent was then refused 'this worktree is already bound to ...'. Fix in the MCP dispatcher: the connection's location belongs to the connection's identity; a claim under a different per-call identity is not standing there, so it does not adopt (it creates its own tree, as the CLI from the primary does). An as_agent equal to the connection's own identity (declared or derived) still adopts. Items already bound keep their recorded tree (rebound path), so live bindings are untouched.
data.title: ddflow_claim under an as_agent other than the connection's identity creates its own tree instead of adopting the connection's harness worktree (fixes bug B7c7a0d9222)

data.claim: The MCP dispatcher passes the connection's called_from (the server's start tree = parent's harness worktree) to api.claim for every caller; claim's adopt_existing branch then W.current(called_from) adopts it regardless of the per-call identity.
data.falsifier: A claim with as_agent='sub-1' from Server(repo, called_from=<linked tree>) on unfixed main records adopted=False
data.mechanism: surfaces/mcp.py Server.handle: spec wants_called_from -> called_from=self.called_from; api/lifecycle.py claim: adopted = W.current(called_from or repo) if cfg.worktree.adopt_existing
data.probe: PYTHONPATH=<main> pytest tests/test_asagent_claim.py (against main bbbe066 and again on the branch with mcp.py reverted)
data.probe_output: FAILED test_a_subagents_claim_does_not_adopt_the_parents_tree: AssertionError: sub-1's item adopted the parent's tree ../parent-tree; 1 failed, 4 passed
data.question: Why does an as_agent claim over MCP bind the subagent's item to the parent's harness worktree?

evidence.note: Research CONFIRMED with probe: tests/test_asagent_claim.py::test_a_subagents_claim_does_not_adopt_the_parents_tree fails on unfixed main (adopted parent's tree ../parent-tree) and on the branch with mcp.py reverted; passes with the fix.

data.rule: For unit_tests, run uv run pytest from the worktree with PYTHONPATH unset (env -u PYTHONPATH); never pin PYTHONPATH=<tree> for the full suite
data.title: Run the suite without a PYTHONPATH pinned at the source tree: test_build_probe then probes the source, not the wheel, and fails
data.why: tests/test_build_probe.py runs scripts/ci/build-probe in a subprocess that inherits PYTHONPATH; pointed at a checkout it imports the source and reports 'probed the source tree, not the wheel', a false failure

evidence.note: Probed by tests/test_asagent_claim.py: (a) foreign as_agent -> own tree, second subagent no longer refused; (b) as_agent == declared connection identity -> adopts; (c) as_agent == derived identity -> adopts; (d) no as_agent -> adopts; (e) an item already bound to the parent tree keeps it on re-claim under as_agent (rebound path precedes adoption), so the live B-local-config-surfaces binding was never at risk. Checked by reading: whitespace-only as_agent -> per_call '' -> not foreign; no_worktree claims untouched; DDFLOW_AGENT counted as the connection's own via _default_agent. Not changed (scope): other called_from tools (gate_run/review/merge/precommit/tests) still use the connection's tree for a per-call identity -- only matters for --no-worktree items; CLI --agent from a harness tree still adopts (no connection identity to compare against).

One helper Server._someone_else reuses _default_agent (the same resolution ddflow_identify reports); no parallel identity resolution added; spec flag adopts_callers_tree sits beside wants_called_from on ddflow_claim only.
